device.title: This device
device.info: Applies to this tablet or phone only.
device.groupInfo: What this device is called in the band and which language it speaks.
device.name: Device name
device.lookInfo: Colours, text and the bar at the top.
device.textSizeInfo: Applies to prompter, live queue, show notes and system status - each widget can override it in its “⋯” menu.
device.pedalsInfo: Bluetooth pedal or keyboard: show, sections, playback, prompter and device commands - momentary, latching or timed.
device.mappingInfo: Pair a Bluetooth pedal (e.g. AirTurn, PageFlip) like a keyboard, then add mappings here. Works on the dashboards. Show and sections are controlled only by whoever may control the show (the master); device commands and prompter paging work on every device.
device.flashInfo: Messages from the stage messenger and hints from the song text ({alert: …}) large across the screen.
device.soundInfo: How this device plays track, click and announcements.
device.outputInfo: Split puts the click on one side of the headphone or line output only and the track (in mono) on the other. With a Y cable or a stereo DI the click side goes to the in-ear mix, the track side to the PA - the audience hears no click. Applies to click and announcements everywhere and to the track in Gig. In Solo practice and the timeline editor the track still plays through an audio element and stays on both sides.
device.storageInfo: Which audio files this device keeps for the songs.
device.appInfo: Version of the StageBoard app and updates from the Stage server.

server.title: Stage server
server.info: This device's connection and what the server does for the whole band.
server.connectionInfo: Which Stage server this device talks to and whether the band data is in sync.
server.activeBandInfo: Which band the Stage server's hardware is using right now. A change affects every device.
server.backupInfo: How the Stage server backs up the band data, and snapshots to take along.

statusBar.orderExplain: Top = more important. When it gets tight, items disappear from the bottom first. Always there and so not in the list: menu (☰), on dashboards the dashboard picker (nine dots), status icon, song title and play time; faults always show their word.
statusBar.title: Status bar

flash.bannerHint: A see-through strip at the top, until tapped or {{seconds}} seconds - the rest stays usable.
flash.fullscreenHint: Across the whole screen, until tapped or {{seconds}} seconds.
flash.offHint: No flash messages on this device.

routing.label: Output
routing.mixedDetail: Track, click and announcements on both sides - as before.
routing.clickLeftDetail: Click and announcements left, the track in mono right.
routing.clickRightDetail: Click and announcements right, the track in mono left.

sync.label: Storage & sync
sync.tooBig: Catalogue too big for “Complete” (more than {{percent}}% of the available storage)
sync.stemsInfo: None: only the stems being practised right now - loaded from the Stage server. Selective: stems of the active setlist and pinned songs. Complete: all.

app.updateFailed: The update could not be loaded - try again later. ({{reason}})
app.devUpdates: Updates for the development build come via adb. The real app gets its updates from the Stage server.
app.current: Up to date - the Stage server has no newer version.
app.none: The Stage server offers no app (or can't be reached).

srv.notPaired: Not paired with a Stage server yet.
srv.overrideWarn: This manual address replaces the automatic one{{automatic}} on this device. If it's no longer right, this device won't reach the Stage server.
srv.addressExplainLabel: Explanation: address of the Stage server
srv.addressExplain: Only needed when this device didn't load the app from the Stage server. Leave it empty or enter the automatic address = automatic.

syncState.cantRepair: Can't repair here - leave the band with “Remove from this device” and join again.

hw.unpaired: Not paired with a Stage server yet - search under System → Stage server.

sw.all: All bands on this Stage server.

adm.title: Admin of “{{band}}”
adm.noAdmins: No admins found in this band.

bk.restoreConfirm: Restore “{{file}}” and merge it with the local data?
bk.snapshotsInfo: Independent of a backup plug-in: a full file dump of this band (songs, setlists, dashboards, profiles, plug-ins, show log) to save and restore locally - ideal before bigger changes or a tour.
bk.noAdmin: No Stage server or no admin login on this device.
bk.removeConfirm: Remove target “{{name}}”? The backups there stay.
bk.serverInfo: Safest with two targets, e.g. USB stick and NAS. A ZFS mirror alone is no backup: what is deleted is gone on the mirror too.
bk.noTarget: No target set up yet - the server isn't backed up.
bk.keyTitle: The server's key for the NAS
bk.keyInfo: Add it once on the NAS to the backup user's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys - then the server needs no password.
bk.folderInfo: USB stick, second disk, ZFS dataset or a NAS share mounted by the system.
bk.sshInfo: The NAS is reached over SSH (rsync) - nothing to mount. Unchanged backing tracks take no space twice.
bk.name: Name
bk.dailyHint: Never while a song is playing - then shortly after.
bk.plugHint: As soon as the stick is there, when the last backup is older than a day.

dbg.copyFailed: Copying not allowed - select the text below.
dbg.title: Diagnostics
dbg.explain: What the app has logged on this device (the last 500 entries since loading) - without cables or developer tools.
dbg.flagsInfo: Write extra detailed entries - switch on for troubleshooting only.

wa.label: Backing track via Web Audio
wa.next: Takes effect with the next song.
wa.info: Gig: track and click on the same audio clock, start exact to the sample, sounds like in practice. Off: through the system's audio player (on some devices with sound effects like Dolby).

xf.label: Transition when jumping
xf.info: Cross-fade of the backing track at the jump or repeat point, on this device. Longer sounds softer, shorter punchier. Default {{ms}} ms.
xf.next: Takes effect with the next jump.

ct.title: Cue timing on this device
ct.explain: Measured only while a song is playing. A cue comes late when the app stands still for longer than {{critical}} ms (lookahead {{lookahead}} ms minus one tick of {{tick}} ms). Scheduler pauses only exist for songs with cues.
ct.none: No measurement yet - play a song in Gig mode.
ct.stalls: App stalls (from 50 ms) during {{min}} min of playback: {{count}} · longest:
ct.handed: · cues handed over: {{count}} · of them late:

st.title: Sync test
st.explain: Marks every full second of server time for {{s}} s - with a MIDI note and/or the real click. Start on every device at once; a laptop at the Stage server measures the offset.
st.channel: MIDI channel (a different one per device)
st.compensateInfo: Off: measures the raw latency (to enter it). On: checks the compensation - the click should then land on the second.
